context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-check (WF-02 Step 1d, rework_count 1) on REQ-218's design, verifying CODE-DESIGNER's fix for the single BLOCKER from step-01b (Logger.info/1 with an unsupported analogy to fetch_tenant_schemas/0, which does not log at all).
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), a tick over 3 tenant schemas calls Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 ZERO times for any of them (each skipped for capacity), the GenServer does not crash, and the next tick (cap restored) resumes normally -- verified by a test asserting the mock/spy call count is exactly 0 during the forced-zero tick and exactly 3 on the following tick

with the global cap forced to admit exactly 1 concurrent unit, a tick still processes all 3 tenant schemas' timer poll-and-fire loop to completion (sequential acquire/release, not a permanent block), confirmed by observing all 3 schemas' poll_and_fire/1 calls occur within that single tick

an admission {:error, :capacity} for one schema's operation within a tick does not prevent a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation, or that SAME schema's OTHER operations, from being attempted later in the same tick -- explicit test forcing capacity exhaustion mid-tick and observing partial, not total, skip

Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, _}) is never called anywhere in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- grep-verified, confirming decision 3's per-tenant-exclusion is actually implemented, not just described

an existing per-operation rescue path (e.g. maybe_run_alert_detection/3's rescue _ -> :ok) still catches its own operation's raise with the new acquire/release wrapped around it -- a test forcing that operation to raise still leaves the admission slot released (no leak) and the tick completes
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Re-read lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md's §1 point 3, §2, and §7 Q2 against the rework claim in step-01c, then spot-checked both cited precedent call sites directly rather than trusting the rework's description.

(1) lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:37 and :44 read directly: both are `{:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}` / `{:error, :tenant_schema_missing}` branches inside an `Enum.reduce_while` backfill loop, each calling `Logger.warning(...)` and then returning `{:cont, {:ok, %{counts | skipped: counts.skipped + 1}}}` -- confirmed skip-this-one-continue-the-loop shape, confirmed `Logger.warning/1` (not `:info`), exactly as the rework and the design doc claim.

(2) lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:588 read directly (with surrounding `resolve_auth_header/1` context, lines 575-594): the `with`/`else` fallback branch calls `Logger.warning("alert hook auth_secret_ref resolution failed, sending without Authorization", component: "alert_delivery", ref: ref)` then returns `nil`, degrading gracefully rather than halting delivery -- confirmed `Logger.warning/1`, confirmed degrade-and-continue shape, exactly as claimed.

(3) Design doc re-read in full: §1 point 3 (line 147), §2 (lines 174, 180-198), and §7 Q2 (lines 452-457) all now say `Logger.warning/1` with these two file:line citations, and §2 explicitly states why the prior fetch_tenant_schemas/0 analogy does not hold (its :error path only calls MetricsRegistry.mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0, no logging at all) and that Logger.info/1 has zero live call sites in lib/letflow/. Logger.error's reservation for actual failures (alerts.ex:201, :534) is also correctly distinguished. The single BLOCKER from step-01b is resolved with real, on-point, verified precedent rather than an analogy.

(4) Untouched-elsewhere check: §7 Q1 (maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, REQ-194, correctly left out of scope) and Q3 (mock/spy AC1 wording, correctly flagged for TEST-DESIGNER) read identically to my own step-01b resolution of them -- no unauthorized changes, no new open questions introduced, no drift.

(5) No implementation code re-check: full document scan confirms zero def/defp bodies or control-flow fragments presented as real code -- still signatures, @spec/@type shapes, and prose only, matching the prior PASS-eligible state on every other check from step-01b (insertion granularity, both other open questions, after-clause release-guarantee tracing, AC coverage) which remain valid since nothing in those sections was touched by this rework.

All 6 ACs remain mapped as confirmed in step-01b (AC1->§1/§2/§6, AC2->§1/§3/§6, AC3->§3/§6, AC4->§1 table+§6, AC5->§1 point 2+§6, AC6->§6, deferred to ELIXIR-DEV to run and quote). No remaining gaps. Design is ready for implementation.
